about.metaTitle: About Z & Alpha — Research, Connection, Taking Action
about.heroSubline: for Generation Z & Alpha — knowledgeable and safe in the digital environment
about.introBody: Z & Alpha Initiative is a pioneering project in Vietnam, dedicated to enhancing digital awareness, digital skills, and mental well-being for young people in the technology era. We believe that a healthy digital world can only be built when the younger generations are equipped with deep knowledge, empathy, and enduring human values.
about.missionBody: Z & Alpha Initiative operates at the intersection of research, education, and policy, aiming to build a healthy digital environment for the next generations.
about.pillarsLead: Our work spans three reinforcing pillars:
about.pillar1Body: In-depth research on the social, psychological and behavioural impacts of the digital environment on adolescents, filling the gap in Vietnamese empirical data and international comparison.
about.pillar2Body: Evidence-based policy proposals and recommendations for schools, parents and regulators on protecting children and adolescents in the digital environment.
about.pillar3Body: Training programmes, workshops and communication campaigns that raise community awareness of safe, healthy social media use; equipping young people with digital literacy and alternative activities to reduce reliance on social media.

activitiesEducation.title: Education
activitiesEducation.lead: Z & Alpha partners with educational institutions to deliver awareness programmes, digital-skills training, and hands-on activities that help reduce the impact of social media on young people.
activitiesEducation.pillarsLead: Three reinforcing pillars that build comprehensive digital capability for adolescents.
activitiesEducation.pillar1Body: Equip young people with awareness of how persuasive technology shapes behaviour and mental health — so they can choose actively instead of being led.
activitiesEducation.pillar2Body: A digital-literacy framework based on UNESCO's Digital Kids Asia–Pacific: safety, agency, emotional intelligence and creativity in the digital environment.
activitiesEducation.pillar3Body: Design interactive offline experiences — art, science, reading — to make up for and reduce dependence on social media.
activitiesEducation.chtLead: Four modules adapted from the Center for Humane Technology programme, helping students understand why technology operates the way it does today.
activitiesEducation.chtMod1Body: Why do tech companies compete for our attention? How do those financial incentives shape the design of products we use every day, and how do they harm individuals and society?
activitiesEducation.chtMod2Body: Explore the subtle design choices in social media products — how they capture attention and change user behaviour by design.
activitiesEducation.chtMod3Body: Our minds and bodies have vulnerabilities that can be exploited. Persuasive technology targets exactly those weak points — while social media companies remain indifferent to user well-being.
activitiesEducation.chtMod4Body: Understanding the harms of persuasive technology and the systemic forces driving it, we can begin to imagine how to build humane technology — one that serves the common good.
activitiesEducation.unescoLead: Output of the Digital Kids Asia–Pacific project led by UNESCO in partnership with UNICEF and other stakeholders.
activitiesEducation.unesco1Body: The capacity to protect oneself, personal data and mental health against digital risks.
activitiesEducation.unesco2Body: The capacity to use technology to learn, communicate and contribute positively to community.
activitiesEducation.unesco3Body: The capacity to understand one's own and others' emotions, and to sustain healthy relationships in digital spaces.
activitiesEducation.unesco4Body: The capacity to use technology as a tool for creating content, ideas and new solutions.
activitiesEducation.altLead: Children grow through real-world experience. Z & Alpha designs and runs activities that restore the experiences social media takes away.
activitiesEducation.altArtBody: More than creative skill — art is a space where children express emotions that ordinary language cannot capture. Drawing, writing, performing or making with their own hands gives young people room to process feeling, lower stress and build a sense of agency.
activitiesEducation.altReadingBody: Reading is one of the lowest-cost activities with the deepest brain benefits — vocabulary, attention, critical thinking. For a generation raised on screens, reading is also intentional 'digital detox' for the mind.
activitiesEducation.altScienceBody: Science awakens curiosity — when a child asks 'why?' and is guided to find the answer themselves, they experience the joy of discovery. It is a deeper, more lasting feeling than the instant gratification of social media, and teaches them to face uncertainty calmly.
activitiesEducation.quoteText: Children grow up through real-world experience.

activitiesPolicy.title: Policy recommendations
activitiesPolicy.lead: Evidence-based policy proposals and recommendations for schools, parents and regulatory bodies.
activitiesPolicy.featuredTitle: Social media and the mental health of children and adolescents: An urgent issue requiring action
activitiesPolicy.contextP1: In the digital era, social media has become inseparable from the lives of children and adolescents. Beyond communication and entertainment, it now shapes identity, supports career development and builds social relationships.
activitiesPolicy.contextP2: Yet the prevalence of social media also brings concerning negative impacts — especially on mental health, attention for learning, and the holistic development of young people. Manifestations such as social anxiety, image pressure, FOMO and cyberbullying are increasingly common.
activitiesPolicy.intlLead: Many countries have rolled out decisive policy to protect adolescents in the digital environment.
activitiesPolicy.intl1Body: Parliament passed a law banning under-16s from using social media, slated to apply from December 2025, with fines up to AUD 50 million for non-compliant platforms.
activitiesPolicy.intl2Body: From March 2026, students from primary through high school are banned from using smartphones in classrooms.
activitiesPolicy.intl3Body: Parliament is proposing a ban on social media for under-15s following a thorough inquiry into the negative effects of digital platforms.
activitiesPolicy.vnBody: Initial studies and forums have documented the impact of social media on adolescent mental health. However, there is still a lack of empirical data, concrete scientific evidence and clear policy recommendations for parents, schools, regulators and technology platforms.
activitiesPolicy.goalsLead: The conference is organised to create an academic and policy forum to:
activitiesPolicy.goal1: Share international experience and existing research findings.
activitiesPolicy.goal3: Propose policy, education and communication solutions to protect mental health for children and adolescents in the digital environment.
activitiesPolicy.discussion1: What solutions should Vietnam deploy to raise awareness and reduce social-media risks for children and adolescents?
activitiesPolicy.discussion2: What are the priority actions for the next 5–10 years?
activitiesPolicy.discussion3: How can we strengthen cross-sector coordination between the state, schools, families, society and technology platforms?
